page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, executing one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 16.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, while AVX-512 extensions are absent. The configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2688.98, placing it in the top quartile of tested instances. Multi-core performance aligns with expected 4-core scaling, reaching a multi-core score of 10692.23 in stress-ng and 4962.0 in Geekbench. Cached memory read bandwidth peaks at 498.39 GB/sec, dropping to 48.77 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 34.91 GB/sec for writes. Workloads involving multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving yield weaker metrics relative to the field, recording 34.81 GB/sec and 5.44 GB/sec respectively.

The 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation provides predictable CPU execution and eliminates noisy neighbor issues stemming from hyperthreading. Because it lacks local NVMe disks, storage needs must be serviced via network-attached block storage. The t2d-standard-4 represents an efficient hardware profile for web application servers, containerized microservices, build pipelines, and general business logic where consistent per-core compute performance is required without the operational overhead of shared hardware threads.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs running on 4 physical cores without hyperthreading, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory for a standard 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is not included, and no hardware GPU accelerators are present. Across performance benchmarks, the instance shows strong single-core compute execution, placing in the top quartile for single-core stress-ng tests, alongside mid-range multi-core processing, memory throughput, and in-memory database operations. The lack of simultaneous multithreading ensures predictable execution for core-bound tasks, though multi-threaded decompression and static web delivery throughput test lower than comparable configurations. The t2d-standard-4 serves well for standard enterprise workloads, intermediate data processing, container hosting, and general web applications requiring reliable per-core throughput.
